text:
maria: Quick heads-up — I'm seeing a 12-18% latency regression on paged-attn for long-prefix (4k+) sessions after yesterday's KV pager allocator tweak. Repro script attached, but wanted to surface here first.

jonathan: ugh. which tweak exactly? the slab split threshold change?

maria: yes — lowered slab_split_threshold from 0.25 -> 0.15 to reduce OOMs. It reduced peak memory but increased tail latency. profile shows more frequent blocktable scans.

lee: Can you paste the flame graph or perf output?

maria: pasted TL;DR below. main differences: more time in paged_attn::block_table::scan_evictions and memcpy on hot paths. Kernel selection still chooses flash-variant, but batch sizes fell ~20% under same qps.

maria: ````
# baseline (master before tweak)
avg p99: 72ms
batch size median: 16
block_table scan time: 3.2% CPU

# after tweak
avg p99: 86ms
batch size median: 13
block_table scan time: 9.8% CPU
````

sophia: interesting — reducing split threshold probably made more partial blocks, so slotmap lookups go up. That explains batch size drop: more fragmented KV pages -> more IO jitter -> scheduling backs off.

jonathan: @maria can you run the microbench for allocation hotpath? i want the allocator op counts (alloc/free/handoff) per second with the new params.

maria: ran it: allocs +23%, frees +15%, handoffs +40% (handoffs are spiking on multi-tenant runs). logs below.

maria: ````
alloc_counts: 128k/s
free_counts: 105k/s
handoff_counts: 46k/s
avg slab occupancy: 66%
avg fragmentation: 18%
````

lee: That handoff spike smells like increased cross-shard reclamation. We recently changed the prefetch heuristics to avoid stalling kernels; maybe it interacts with the slab split.

sophia: Another angle: kernel chooser penalizes suspected OOM-prone kernels by reducing inflight windows. If fragmentation rises, we may be hitting the "kernel_safety" path that throttles batches. Check the chooser logs for fallback penalties.

maria: chooser shows periodic penalty entries for flash-16k variant between 11:02-11:18 — coincides with the increased block_table scans.

jonathan: Two hypotheses: 1) more partial pages -> more metadata ops -> scan cost up; 2) split threshold increases remote-ish allocations, causing slower returns and backpressure. Both hurt batching.

lee: Quick mitigation idea: bump slab_split_threshold back to 0.22 and enable a soft-merge pass every N seconds to coalesce small blocks lazily. That should reduce fragmentation without risking OOM bursts.

maria: I can try that in a canary cluster. If it recovers p99 and batch size, we can keep it until we have a better long-term allocator rework.

sophia: Also request we instrument block_table scanning: add a lightweight counter for "scan_iterations" and time-per-scan binning (<=50us, 50-200us, >200us). Will help pinpoint pathological cases.

jonathan: Good. Add a short perf test: long-prefix synthetic (8k tokens) + 4 concurrent sessions, run for 5m. Capture kernel-chooser logs, batching histograms, and allocator op rates.

maria: will run now on canary-2. ETA 20m.

deploy-bot: deploy start: paged-attn/canary-2 @ maria (rev patched-slab-merge-2026-03-18)

maria: ran the canary. Results: p99 down to 75ms, batch size median back to 15, handoffs -18%. Fragmentation dropped to 11%. Full logs uploaded to the infra bucket: s3://redwood-infra/perf/3165432109/

maria: ````
canary summary:
- slab_split_threshold: 0.22
- soft_merge_interval: 30s
- p99: 75ms (was 86ms)
- batch median: 15
- handoffs: 38k/s -> 31k/s
- fragmentation: 11%
````

lee: Nice! That looks promising. Any regression on memory spike/OOMs?

maria: no OOMs in the 1h soak. Peak memory +4% but within cushion for canary.

jonathan: Operationally, let's ship the slab_split_threshold bump + soft_merge to prod only after 24h soak and a run of perf regression suite. Sophia, can you add the scan instrumentation in a small PR? Should be minimal.

sophia: On it. I'll add counters + histograms and a small unit test that simulates heavy partial-page churn.

maria: Action items:
- maria: run 24h soak and post aggregated histograms (kernel chooser, batch sizes, alloc ops)
- sophia: PR for block_table scan telemetry + unit test
- jonathan: add a quick kernel-chooser experiment to see if tweak changes fallback frequency over longer runs

jonathan: one more note — we should also check if batching heuristic can be slightly more aggressive when we detect low fragmentation. If we can safely increase inflight window by +10% when fragmentation < 12% it might reclaim some latency.

lee: agree but prefer to keep chooser conservative until we confirm stability. Maybe an adaptive knob behind a feature flag.

maria: thanks team. I'll file the follow-ups and post numbers in #eng-runtime after the 24h soak. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy success: paged-attn/canary-2 @ maria (rev patched-slab-merge-2026-03-18)
